title: Lubia polo
subtitle: Persian green bean and lamb rice
excerpt: Lubia polo is a Persian rice dish with green beans, lamb mince, tomato, and spices layered through the grains and steamed together. The beans and meat cook into the rice during the long steam, and the whole thing comes out fragrant and richly coloured with turmeric and tomato.
sourceNotes: Najmieh Batmanglij, Food of Life: Ancient Persian and Modern Iranian Cooking and Ceremonies (1986). Lubia polo documented as a popular mixed rice dish. Margaret Shaida, The Legendary Cuisine of Persia (1992). Notes on the layering technique and the importance of parboiling the rice first.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: The lamb and bean mixture can be cooked up to two days ahead. Parboil the rice and assemble on the day.

content.text: Lubia polo is Persian layered rice with green beans and spiced lamb. The lamb is cooked first with tomato, turmeric, and cinnamon into a rich, fragrant mixture, then layered with parboiled basmati through the pot before the long steam. The tahdig crust forms at the base and the whole thing is turned out onto a platter so the golden crust sits on top.

items.prepNote: trimmed and cut into 3 cm pieces

content.text: Cook the lamb and green bean mixture

Heat {{olive-oil}} in a large frying pan. Add {{onion}} and fry for ten minutes until golden. Add {{lamb-mince}} and cook for five minutes until browned, breaking it up. Add {{turmeric-ground}}, {{cinnamon-ground}}, {{allspice}}, {{tomato-puree}}, and {{sea-salt-fine}}. Stir well and cook for two minutes.
Add {{green-beans}} and 100 ml of water. Cover and cook for ten minutes until the beans are just tender and the liquid absorbed. Taste and adjust seasoning. Set aside.
Parboil {{basmati-rice}} in salted boiling water for six to seven minutes until just tender outside but chalky within. Drain in a colander.

Heat {{sunflower-oil}} and 3 tablespoons of water in a large heavy saucepan over medium-high heat. Spread a thin layer of drained rice over the base. Add a layer of the lamb and bean mixture, then rice, alternating until all is used. End with rice.

Wrap the lid in a clean tea towel and place firmly on the pan. Cook on medium-high for three minutes to build steam, then on the lowest heat for 30 to 35 minutes. Rest on a cold wet cloth for two minutes. Spoon the rice mixture onto a platter and invert the tahdig crust on top.

items.symptom: The green beans have gone mushy
items.cause: Cooked for too long in the lamb mixture before steaming
items.fix: Cook the beans for ten minutes only: they should be just tender. They will soften further in the steam.

items.symptom: The rice is sticking together in the pot
items.cause: Insufficient oil or not rinsed well
items.fix: Rinse the rice until the water runs clear. The oil must coat the base fully before the rice goes in.
Drop to the lowest heat immediately after the three-minute steam build. Use a heat diffuser if available.

items.symptom: The lamb and bean mixture has dried out
items.cause: Not enough liquid in the initial cook
items.fix: The mixture should be moist but not wet when assembling. Add a splash of water if it looks dry before layering.

content.text: Lubia polo sits within the large Persian category of mixed rice dishes called polow, where vegetables, fruit, or meat are layered through parboiled rice and steamed together. The combination of green beans and lamb is a classic summer polow, made when French beans are at their best. It is everyday home cooking in Iran, less ceremonial than zereshk polo (barberry rice) but satisfying and complete as a meal on its own. Served with mast-o musir and a simple salad, it needs nothing else.
